title: Helen Humes
summary: Greene liked Helen Humes as a good band singer who fit the band.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Of course, in a way -- Basie didn't need two singers, did he? I mean, really -- I would have thought --
Well, he -- Billy was like the first singer, more or less, and then I think Helen Humes came second.
Yeah, but I think Stan means Rushing was --
Oh, you mean with Jimmy Rushing. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
Because Helen, I mean -- all the records -- and she never got any good songs to sing. She always had awful songs.
I liked her. She sounded good.
Yes, she did. She suited nicely the band, didn't she?
Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
She had a good rhythmic thing for the band, didn't she?
Yeah. Yeah.
And, she was sort of -- had sort of an easy-going attitude, and what-not, didn't she?
Helen -- I think she sounded good with the band. I think she fit with the band -- you know what I mean? And, it would have been a good thing if she had stayed, you know?
Yeah.
The longer in a lot of ways she stayed ... we would've gotten tighter, and the public ...
Yeah.
Yeah. And, the thing was about Helen, too, was that it didn't -- she was a good band singer.
Mm hmm.
And, it didn't have to be a big thing -- a big production.
No, no, no.
You know -- there wasn't, like, a thing about billing, and all that.
No. No.
There wasn't trouble with it, you know. She was a good band singer, and she was used that way and it worked out great.
Yeah.
From the point of view of listening to her, I think it was great, wasn't it?
Yeah.
